body.statement: Given the proved uniform first-order expansion and singular Gaussian approximation for the same-sample estimated-\(A\) cumulant process, can one construct implementable Gaussian or bootstrap critical values that yield asymptotically calibrated, nonconservative Anderson--Rubin inversion uniformly through singular and rank-changing influence covariance, including distributions with atoms at candidate critical values?
body.justification: This is the principal remaining proof boundary between the proved conservative rate-optimal inversion and implementable covariance-adaptive calibration.
body.gap: Long et al. treat regular environmental GMM, Andrews and Guggenberger treat supplied singular moments, and Davis--Kahan perturbation theory controls projector stability; none derives a uniform cumulant U-statistic expansion through a same-sample estimated spectral projector.
body.consumer: A solution gives practitioners nonconservative calibrated confidence sets when the flag is weak and the projected moment covariance loses or changes rank.
